t1498.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥammād ibn Zayd al-Azdī al-Jahḍamī, Abū Ismāʿīl al-Baṣrī, as reliable, firm, and a jurist; one of the senior eighth generation, he died in year seventy-nine at eighty-one.
as: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أئمة الناس في زمانهم أربعة: سفيان الثوري بالكوفة، ومالك بالحجاز، والأوزاعي بالشام، وحماد بن زيد بالبصرة
The imams of the people in their time were four: al-Thawrī in Kufa, Mālik in the Hijaz, al-Awzāʿī in Syria and Ḥammād ibn Zayd in Basra.
عبيد الله بن الحسن, quoted by al-Mizzī
إنما هما الحمادان، فإذا طلبتم العلم فاطلبوه من الحمادين
It is only the two Ḥammāds; when you seek knowledge, seek it from them.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت أعلم من حماد بن زيد، ولا من سفيان، ولا من مالك
I have not seen anyone more knowledgeable than Ḥammād ibn Zayd, Sufyān or Mālik.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت أحدا لم يكتب الحديث أحفظ من حماد بن زيد، ولم يكن عنده كتاب إلا جزء ليحيى بن سعيد وكان يخلط فيه
Of those who did not write hadith, none had a better memory than Ḥammād; he had no book except a part from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, in which he used to confuse things.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
لم أر أحدا قط أعلم بالسنة، ولا بالحديث الذي يدخل في السنة من حماد بن زيد
I never saw anyone more knowledgeable of the Sunnah and the hadith bearing on it than Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Mahdī, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت بالبصرة أفقه من حماد بن زيد
I did not see anyone in Basra with more fiqh than Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
يزيد بن زريع, quoted by al-Mizzī
أيهما أثبت في الحديث؟ قال: حماد بن زيد، وكان الآخر رجلا صالحا
Asked which of the two Ḥammāds was firmer in hadith, he said Ḥammād ibn Zayd; the other was a righteous man.
حماد بن زيد، ما كنا نشبه حماد بن زيد إلا بمسعر
Ḥammād ibn Zayd (had the better memory); we likened him only to Misʿar.
يحيى بن يحيى, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت أحدا من الشيوخ أحفظ من حماد بن زيد
I have not seen any shaykh with a better memory than Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
حماد بن زيد أحب إلينا من عبد الوارث، حماد بن زيد من أئمة المسلمين من أهل الدين والإسلام، وهو أحب إلي من حماد بن سلمة
Ḥammād ibn Zayd is dearer to us than ʿAbd al-Wārith; he is one of the imams of the Muslims, people of religion, and dearer to me than Ḥammād ibn Salamah.
كان ضريرا، وكان يحفظ حديثه كله
He was blind and memorised all his hadith.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
حماد بن زيد أثبت من عبد الوارث، وابن علية، وعبد الوهاب الثقفي، وابن عيينة
Ḥammād ibn Zayd is firmer than ʿAbd al-Wārith, Ibn ʿUlayyah, ʿAbd al-Wahhāb al-Thaqafī and Ibn ʿUyaynah.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ليس أحد في أيوب أثبت من حماد بن زيد
No one is firmer in Ayyūb's hadith than Ḥammād ibn Zayd.
سليمان بن حرب, quoted by al-Mizzī
حماد بن زيد في أيوب أكبر من كل من روى عن أيوب
In Ayyūb's hadith Ḥammād ranks above everyone who narrated from Ayyūb.
Yaḥyā ibn Maʿīn, quoted by al-Mizzī
ومن خالفه من الناس جميعا في أيوب فالقول قوله
Whoever of all people differs with him on Ayyūb, his word prevails.
Abū Zurʿah al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
حماد بن زيد أثبت من حماد بن سلمة بكثير، وأصح حديثا، وأتقن
Ḥammād ibn Zayd is much firmer than Ḥammād ibn Salamah, sounder in hadith and more precise.
مات حماد بن زيد يوم مات، ولا أعلم له في الإسلام نظيرا في هيئته، ودله
When Ḥammād died I knew of no equal to him in Islam in his bearing and manner.
ايت حماد بن زيد فخذ العلم بحلم
(Verse:) Go to Ḥammād ibn Zayd and take knowledge with forbearance.
خالد بن خداش, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان حماد بن زيد من عقلاء الناس وذوي الألباب
Ḥammād ibn Zayd was among the wise and intelligent people.
يزيد بن زريع, quoted by al-Mizzī
Today the master of the Muslims has died.
وكان ثقة ثبتا حجة كثير الحديث
He was reliable, firm, an authority, with many hadiths.
يرون أن حماد بن زيد دون شعبة في الحديث
They consider Ḥammād ibn Zayd below Shuʿbah in hadith.
عبد الله بن معاوية الجمحي, quoted by al-Mizzī
وفضل ابن سلمة على ابن زيد كفضل الدينار علي الدرهم
Ibn Salamah's superiority over Ibn Zayd is like the dinar's over the dirham.
وكان عثمانيا. وكان ثقة ثبتا حجة كثير الحديث
He held ʿUthmānī views. He was reliable, firm in transmission, an authority whose reports count as evidence, and prolific in hadith.

t1911.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Rabīʿa ibn Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Taymī, Abū ʿUthmān al-Madanī, known as Rabīʿat al-Raʾy, trustworthy and a famous jurist, of the fifth generation. Ibn Saʿd said people were wary of him for his use of opinion. He died in 36 AH, per the sound view, or 3, or 42 per al-Bājī.
as: They were wary of him because of his use of personal opinion (raʾy).
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
Trustworthy, though Abū al-Zinād was more learned than him.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
Yaʿqūb ibn Shaybah, quoted by al-Mizzī
Trustworthy and firm, one of the muftis of Medina.
Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd al-Qaṭṭān, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت أحدا أفطن من ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
I have seen no one sharper than Rabīʿah.
عبيد الله بن عمر, quoted by al-Mizzī
He is the one for our hard problems, our scholar and the best of us.
سوار بن عبد الله العنبري, quoted by al-Mizzī
ما رأيت أحدا أعلم من ربيعة الرأي
I have seen no one more learned than Rabīʿat al-Raʾy, not even al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn.
عبد العزيز بن أبو سلمة, quoted by al-Mizzī
والله ما رأيت أحدا أحفظ لسنة منه
By God, I have seen no one who preserved the Sunnah better than him.
الحافظ أبو بكر بن ثابت, quoted by al-Mizzī
كان فقيها عالما حافظا للفقه والحديث
He was a jurist and scholar who preserved law and hadith.
وكان ثقة، كثير الحديث، وكانوا يتقونه لموضع الرأي
He was trustworthy with many hadiths, but people were wary of him because of his use of opinion (raʾy).
Mālik ibn Anas, quoted by al-Mizzī
ذهبت حلاوه الفقه منذ مات ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن
The sweetness of jurisprudence has gone since Rabīʿah died.
عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم, quoted by al-Mizzī
مكث ربيعة دهرا طويلا عابدا يصلي الليل والنهار صاحب عباده
Rabīʿah spent a long time devoted to worship and praying night and day.

t6820.bio: Ibn Ḥajar calls Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā al-Ashjaʿī al-Madanī trustworthy and firmly established; Abū Ḥātim said he was the most reliable of Mālik's associates. Of the senior tenth generation, he died in 198.
as: He is the most firmly established of Mālik's companions.
Abū Ḥātim al-Rāzī, quoted by al-Mizzī
أثبت أصحاب مالك وأوثقهم معن بن عيسى، وهو أحب إلي من عبد الله بن نافع الصائغ، ومن ابن وهب
Maʿn ibn ʿĪsā was the most precise and reliable of Mālik’s students. I prefer him to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ al-Ṣāʾigh and Ibn Wahb.
وكان ثقة، كثير الحديث، ثبتا. مأمونا
He was reliable, prolific in hadith, precise, and trustworthy.
Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, quoted by al-Mizzī
I did not write anything from Maʿn.
وكان ثقة كثير الحديث ثبتا مأمونا
He was reliable, prolific in hadith, precise, and trustworthy.

t8105.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū Zuhayr al-Thaqafī as a Companion with a ḥadīth, identified as Muʿādh ibn Rabāḥ, with disagreement over his name.

t8170.bio: Ibn Ḥajar describes Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Ḥārithī, also called al-Khāzin or al-Ḥādī, as acceptable and of the fifth generation.

t8268.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū ʿUmar, also called Abū ʿAmr, al-Ghadānī al-Baṣrī as acceptable, of the third generation; one who said his name is Yaḥyā ibn ʿUbayd erred.

t8286.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Abū ʿAnabah al-Khawlānī, said to be named ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAnabah or ʿUmārah, as a Companion with a report; it is also said he accepted Islam in the Prophet's time without seeing him, settled in Ḥimṣ, and died under ʿAbd al-Malik.

t8422.bio: Ibn Ḥajar gives Abū Hārūn al-Ghanawī as Ibrāhīm ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, calls him reliable, places him in the sixth generation, and notes one passage of his in al-Bukhārī on funerals.

t8497.bio: Ibn Ḥajar says the nephew of Ṣafiyya bint Ḥuyayy is not known and belongs to the third generation. Abū Dāwūd transmits from him.
as: Not known, of the third generation.

t8589.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Rumaytha bint al-Ḥārith al-Azdiyya, sister of ʿAwf, foster-brother of ʿĀʾisha, described as maqbūla and belonging to the fourth generation.

t8794.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Ḥuṣayn ibn Muḥṣin or ʿUbayd Allāh ibn Muḥṣin al-Anṣārī, from a paternal aunt of his said to be named Asmāʾ; she is a Companion with a hadith.

t932.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Jaʿfar ibn Burqān al-Kilābī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Raqqī, as ṣadūq but erring in al-Zuhrī's hadith; of the seventh generation, died 50 AH or later.
as: Truthful/acceptable, but errs in his transmission from al-Zuhrī.

t987.bio: Ibn Ḥajar records Juwaybir ibn Saʿīd al-Azdī, Abū al-Qāsim al-Balkhī, resident of Kūfah, transmitter of tafsīr, as very weak, of the fifth generation; he died after the fortieth year.
